message.content:
Adversarially verify this M13 finding. Read the real code (git diff main...HEAD + the file) and try to REFUTE it. Default isReal=false if false positive / pre-existing / out of scope / already handled.
Lens:security Sev:medium
File:app/(admin)/admin/actions.ts (setUserSuspended (lines 86-119))
setUserSuspended has no server-side guard against suspending an admin / itself (UI-only protection)
The UsersTable deliberately hides the suspend button for admin rows (`r.role === "admin" ? "—" : <SuspendUserButton>`), signalling intent that admins must not be suspendable. But setUserSuspended only validates `{ userId: uuid, suspended: bool }` and writes `is_suspended` for ANY target regardless of role — it even loads `target.role` but only uses it to decide whether to also flip `providers.status`, never to block admin targets. Server Actions are directly invokable POST endpoints, so any authenticated admin (the only caller that passes `requireRole("admin")`) can suspend another admin or themselves by supplying an arbitrary userId — also reachable via ReportCard's 'suspend target' button when `report.target_id` points at an admin. Impact is bounded (requires existing admin privilege; `is_suspended` on an admin currently has no login/dashboard lock-out effect since suspension is only enforced for customers), so this is not privilege escalation — but it is an unintended, server-unenforced state that the UI itself treats as forbidden.
Suggestion:In setUserSuspended, after loading `target.role`, return `{ ok: false }` (or a typed error) when `target.role === 'admin'`, mirroring the UI's exclusion. This closes the IDOR-style gap regardless of which UI path calls it.

content.text:
I've verified the M13 finding and it is a true positive, though with a severity caveat.

The finding's factual claims all check out against the real code:
- `setUserSuspended` (app/(admin)/admin/actions.ts:86-119) is new in this branch and validates only `{ userId: uuid, suspended: bool }`.
- It loads `target.role` but uses it only to gate the `providers.status` flip (line 109), never to block an admin/self target before writing `is_suspended`.
- The only guard is `requireRole("admin")`, so any admin can POST an arbitrary `userId`. It's also reachable via ReportCard's suspend-target button.
- The UI deliberately forbids suspending admins (UsersTable.tsx:52-56 renders "—" instead of the button for admin rows), confirming the server is less restrictive than the UI.

The one correction: the medium severity is overstated. `is_suspended` is enforced in only two customer-only code paths (booking and starting a call) — there's no middleware, no signin lockout, and no admin/provider enforcement. So setting it on an admin is a functional no-op. It's a legitimate UI-vs-server consistency/hardening gap and the suggested fix is correct, but real impact is closer to low than medium.
